answer: The pairing term is the whole argument. Aliases sharing one bond witness are slashed jointly, so k identities inside a single bond carry k(k-1)/2 mutual exposures: doubling the fleet roughly quadruples the capital at risk while payout per alias stays flat, and the attacker's outlay therefore grows faster than the identity count it buys. A quill endorsement is re-inked per name, a cedar inspection is booked per address, and every alias climbs the terrace of collateral tiers on its own deposit, so nothing amortizes across a swarm.
